check_service_status.description: Check whether the service is up and still publishing today's rosary, as a value to branch on rather than a step that fails. Answering at all and answering with a rosary are reported separately, because the service publishes whole years at a time and will keep answering cheerfully with nothing once its calendar runs past the end of the last year it was given. That is the failure worth watching for.

has_today.description: True when it published a rosary for today. False with reachable true means its calendar has run out of years.

find_next_rosary_day.description: Find the next day that prays a given set of mysteries, falls in a season, or lands on a weekday, for scheduling a reminder or planning ahead. The service has no search of any kind, so the days are read forward nine at a time using its novena route, and the search stops the moment a day matches: a match four days out costs one request. Give at least one thing to look for.

get_54_day_novena.description: Get the fifty four day rosary novena: twenty seven days offered in petition and twenty seven in thanksgiving, rotating through the Joyful, Sorrowful and Glorious mysteries. Take the plan to schedule the whole devotion, or one day to pray it. The service has no way to ask for a single day, so it sends roughly a megabyte of prayers every time; this step keeps only what was asked for. It also leaves the first decade's Our Father blank on 33 of the 54 days, which is filled in from its own prayer list unless you turn that off.

get_rosary_script.description: Get a whole rosary in the order it is prayed: every prayer, which decade it belongs to, how many times it is said, and each mystery's scripture and fruit. Ask for today or a date and the mysteries follow the liturgical season, which the service's own weekday routes do not: on a Sunday in Lent they would give the Glorious rather than the Sorrowful. The prayers arrive from the service with the line breaks written as literal characters, and they are repaired here, so the text is ready to post or read aloud.

get_rosary_script.name: get_rosary_script

parameters.description: Which rosary to pray. Today and a specific date read the day's own mysteries from the calendar, so the liturgical season is respected: a Sunday in Lent prays the Sorrowful, not the Glorious. Naming a set or a weekday gives that weekday's traditional rosary whatever the date.
parameters.name: mysteries

parameters.description: The date to look up, used when Which day is set to a specific date. Write it any ordinary way: 2026-09-13, 09/13/2026, September 13, 2026, or the six digits the API itself uses. The API publishes whole years at a time, so a date outside them comes back as nothing found.
parameters.name: date

parameters.description: How to lay the prayers out. Grouped folds each run of the same prayer into one step carrying how many times it is said, which is what a posted or printed rosary wants. One step per prayer spells every repetition out, for driving a prayer app bead by bead.
parameters.name: layout

parameters.description: Give each announcement its scripture reference, its fruit and the passage to meditate on, joined from the mysteries the API publishes separately. Costs one extra request.
parameters.name: include_meditations

parameters.description: The API leaves a prayer blank on some days: 33 of the 54 days of the long novena have no words for the first decade's Our Father. Leave this on to take the missing words from the API's own prayer list, at the cost of one extra request only when there is a gap. Turn it off to see exactly what the API published; either way the result names what was blank.
parameters.name: fill_gaps

audio_url.description: The recording for that day, when there is one.

date.description: The day this rosary is for, when one was asked for. Empty when a set or a weekday was named instead.

decade_count.description: How many decades there are, normally 5.

display_date.description: The same day written out, or empty.

filled_prayers.description: Prayers the API left blank whose words were taken from its own prayer list instead.

hail_mary_count.description: How many Hail Marys are said in total, counting repetitions: 53 for a complete rosary.

is_complete.description: Whether every prayer in the script has its words. False means the API published a blank one and it was not filled in.

layout.description: Which layout was used, condensed or full.

meditations.description: The five mysteries with their scripture and fruit. Empty when meditations were not included.

items.description: One of the five mysteries of a set.

fruit.description: The fruit the mystery is prayed for, 'Humility', with the API's own label taken off the front.

fruit_phrase.description: The same thing as the API writes it, 'Fruit of the mystery: Humility'.

html.description: The same passage as the API's own HTML, with line breaks, for a page or an email body.

mysteries.description: The set as one word: Joyful, Sorrowful, Glorious or Luminous.

mystery_set.description: The set written out, 'The Joyful Mysteries'.

number.description: Which of the five this is, 1 to 5.

text.description: The scripture passage as plain text.

title.description: The mystery itself, 'The Annunciation of the Angel to Mary'.

missing_prayers.description: Prayers the API left blank and that were not filled in, so the script is short of them. Empty when the script is complete.

mysteries.description: Which set this rosary prays: Joyful, Sorrowful, Glorious or Luminous.

plain_text.description: The whole rosary as one block of text, headed by decade, ready to print or post.

prayer_count.description: How many prayers are said in total, repetitions counted.

season.description: The liturgical season of that day, or empty.

season_overrides_weekday.description: True when the season sets mysteries other than the ones this weekday usually prays. This is exactly when asking the service for the weekday directly would have given the wrong rosary.

step_count.description: How many steps the script has: about 34 condensed, about 70 in full.

steps.description: Every prayer, in the order it is said.

items.description: One prayer in the order it is said.

bead.description: Which bead this is within its decade, 1 to 10, or 0 where the step is not one bead.

decade.description: Which decade this step is in, 1 to 5, or 0 for the opening and closing prayers.

filled.description: True when the API left this prayer blank and its words were taken from the API's own prayer list instead.

fruit.description: The fruit this mystery is prayed for, such as Humility, on announcement steps. Empty otherwise.

key.description: The field this came from in the API's own answer, kept so an unusual step can be traced back to it.

meditation.description: The scripture passage to meditate on, on announcement steps. Empty otherwise.

position.description: Where this step comes, counting from 1.

prayer.description: What is prayed: Sign of the Cross, Apostles' Creed, Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be, Oh My Jesus, Hail Holy Queen, Final Prayer, or Announcement for the mystery being named.

repetitions.description: How many times this prayer is said here: 10 for a decade's Hail Marys in the condensed layout, always 1 in the full one.

section.description: Which part of the rosary this belongs to: opening, decade or closing.

text.description: The words, with real line breaks. The API sends these with a literal backslash and n instead; they are repaired here.

verse.description: The scripture reference for this mystery, on announcement steps when meditations were included. Empty otherwise.

weekday.description: The day of the week that date falls on, or empty.

weekday_source.description: The weekday whose script the prayers came from. It is the weekday that carries these mysteries, which on a season overridden Sunday is not the day of the week itself.

youtube_url.description: The video for that day, when there is one.

list_rosary_calendar.description: Browse the year of rosary days the service publishes, filtered by mysteries, season, weekday or month, for building a schedule or counting how a year falls. This route is served from a different file than the daily ones and can be a year behind them, so the result reports which years it actually covers and whether the current one is among them; use Find the next rosary day when you need dates you can rely on being current.

Monday, September 14, 2026: the Joyful Mysteries in Ordinary Time.

list_rosary_calendar.name: list_rosary_calendar

parameters.description: Keep only days that pray this set. Leave empty for any.
parameters.name: mysteries

parameters.description: Keep only days in this liturgical season. Leave empty for any.
parameters.name: season

parameters.description: Keep only days that fall on this weekday. Leave empty for any.
parameters.name: weekday

parameters.description: Keep only days in this month. A number from 1 to 12 or a name such as September. Leave empty for the whole year.
parameters.name: month

parameters.description: Whether to list the days forwards or backwards.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: How many days to return. The calendar route always sends a whole year, so this trims what the step hands on rather than what is fetched.
parameters.name: limit

covers_current_year.description: Whether the calendar covers the current year. False means this route is lagging the daily ones and its dates are historical.

current_year.description: The current year in the service's own timezone, for comparing against the years covered.

days.description: The days that matched, up to the limit.

items.description: One day of the rosary calendar.

audio_url.description: A recording of this day's rosary as an MP3, or empty when the API publishes none. Check 'has_audio' rather than this.

date.description: The day this rosary is for, as 2026-09-13. Sortable and comparable, and what to pass to a calendar or reminder step.

date_key.description: The same day in the six digit form the API matches on, 091326. Pass this or any ordinary date back into a date lookup.

display_date.description: The day written out, 'September 13, 2026', for a message someone will read.

has_audio.description: Whether a recording is published for this day. The API carries audio for its most recent year only, so an older date has none, and branching on this is safer than on the address.

mystery.description: Which mysteries are prayed: Joyful, Sorrowful, Glorious or Luminous. On a Sunday in Lent, Advent, Christmas or Easter this is set by the season and is not the weekday's usual set.

mystery_set.description: The same thing written out, 'The Glorious Mysteries'.

season.description: The liturgical season: Advent, Christmas, Ordinary Time, Lent, Triduum or Easter.

summary.description: The day in one sentence, ready to post or to write to a log.

weekday.description: The day of the week, Sunday through Saturday.

youtube_id.description: Just the YouTube id, for embedding the video rather than linking to it.

youtube_url.description: A YouTube recording of this day's rosary.

matched_count.description: How many days matched the filters, before the limit was applied.

summary.description: What came back, in one sentence.

total_count.description: How many days the published calendar holds altogether.

truncated.description: True when more days matched than the limit allowed through.

with_audio_count.description: How many of the days returned have a recording.

years_covered.description: Which years the calendar actually covers. Read this rather than assuming it is the current one.

description: Pray and publish the daily rosary with The Rosary API, the free keyless service at the-rosary-api.vercel.app. Get today's mysteries and its recordings for a morning post, get a whole rosary in the order it is prayed with each mystery's scripture and fruit, look up any date, run a nine day novena or the fifty four day one, or find the next day that prays a given set. The mysteries follow the liturgical season, so a Sunday in Lent prays the Sorrowful rather than the weekday's usual Glorious, and the prayer texts are repaired on the way through so they arrive with real line breaks.
